videos.title: Typography Theory: The Anatomy of Type | Basics for Beginners
videos.why: A slow, clearly drawn tour of the parts of a letter; keep lab-type-anatomy open and test yourself on each term before he names it.

videos.title: Hyperlegible: an approach to accessible type design
videos.why: A case study of Atkinson Hyperlegible, made for the Braille Institute; from 4:51 he shows how easily confused letters were redrawn to be distinct, which is letter anatomy used for a real purpose.

podcasts.episode: Design Matters from the Archive: Tobias Frere-Jones
podcasts.why: Debbie Millman talks with the type designer behind Gotham about his career and why typefaces are like the air we breathe; a good way to hear how a type designer thinks about letterforms.

reads.title: An overview of Latin type anatomy
reads.why: The illustrated reference for x-height, baseline, cap height, ascenders and the rest; note the point that a large x-height makes one font look bigger than another at the same size.

reads.title: Making sense of typographic classifications
reads.why: Serif, sans serif, slab, monospaced, script and display explained, with the honest caveat that the groups overlap; read it before you filter Google Fonts for a project.

reads.title: What is good typography?
reads.why: Matthew Butterick's one-page answer, that good typography reinforces the meaning of the text; a test you can apply to every font decision.
